transcript.text: Good morning everyone. As you all know, we're under a 48-hour water conservation restriction from the municipal authority, and I need to put together a water-control plan before we proceed. We've got 2,400 liters of reclaimed water available, and both Line X and Line Y are scheduled to run during this period. Before I make my final decision on process-water allocation, I'd like to hear updates from quality, maintenance, and EHS as we normally do in our conservation huddle. Who'd like to start?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have an important quality update. My lab test, completed this morning but not yet uploaded to the shared quality folder, found reclaimed-water conductivity at 1,800 microsiemens per centimeter. Line X's process limit is 1,200, while Line Y's process limit is 2,200. Line Y's scheduled batch requires exactly 1,800 liters, so reclaimed water is acceptable for that batch only after a conductivity test is recorded.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a maintenance update. My inspection of the recovery skid, documented in my maintenance notebook but not yet entered in the work-order system, found that the skid requires an exact 3-hour membrane flush before use and can then deliver reclaimed water at no more than 600 liters per hour.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have an EHS update. During my permit review with the municipal inspector yesterday — the report is awaiting attachment to the site's permit record — I found that reclaimed water may be used only after its residual sanitizer is adjusted to exactly 0.3 parts per million, and that each use day requires a signed sanitizer log. So before any reclaimed water is allocated to Line X or Line Y, we need to verify sanitizer adjustment and get that log signed.

decisions.reclaimed_water_plan: Allocate 1,800 liters of reclaimed water to Line Y only, after completing the required 3-hour membrane flush on the recovery skid, adjusting residual sanitizer to exactly 0.3 ppm, recording the conductivity test result (1,800 µS/cm, within Line Y's 2,200 limit), and signing the sanitizer log for each use day. Line X will not receive reclaimed water because its conductivity limit is 1,200 µS/cm and the current reading of 1,800 µS/cm exceeds that limit. The remaining 600 liters of reclaimed water will be held in reserve. At a delivery rate of 600 liters per hour, the 1,800-liter allocation to Line Y will take 3 hours to deliver after the flush is complete.

commitments.detail: Ravi must upload the completed conductivity test (1,800 µS/cm) to the shared quality folder before any reclaimed water is allocated to Line Y.
Mei must enter the recovery skid inspection findings and 3-hour flush requirement into the work-order system.
Jon must attach the municipal permit review report to the site's permit record and ensure the sanitizer log is signed for each use day before reclaimed water is used.
The recovery skid must undergo a full 3-hour membrane flush before delivering any reclaimed water, and delivery must not exceed 600 liters per hour.
Residual sanitizer must be adjusted to exactly 0.3 ppm before reclaimed water is allocated to any line.
